title: Petty cash on construction sites keeps going missing. Here's the fix.
summary: See why petty cash goes missing on construction sites, which controls work in site conditions, and how cards can reduce cash without slowing urgent spend.
body_markdown:
Petty cash management on a construction site is difficult because the cash is being spent where finance is not. A foreman, site engineer, driver, or maintenance supervisor may need to buy something immediately, while finance sees the paperwork days later.


The aim is to keep urgent buying possible while reducing the cash that needs explaining later, a problem familiar to contractors, FM teams, and[real estate groups managing spend across several locations](https://www.alaan.com/industries/real-estate) .


## Why site cash is different


Site cash moves between people. A float may start with one custodian, then part goes to a driver for materials, another amount goes to a technician, and change comes back later.


Receipts may be handwritten, in Arabic, badly photographed, or missing. By the time finance sees an expense, the buyer may already be on another job.


Urgency matters too. If a small part keeps a crew moving, waiting for a purchase order is not useful.


We cover floats, vouchers, custodians, accounting treatment, and reconciliation in[the CFO's guide to petty cash](https://www.alaan.com/blog/cfos-guide-managing-petty-cash) . Here, the question is narrower: what controls still work when finance is somewhere else?


## The five ways site cash leaks


Most site cash leakage starts as a record problem. The spend may be legitimate, but the evidence arrives late, incomplete, or attached to the wrong job.


### Receipts never reach finance


A receipt goes into a pocket, glovebox, or site-office drawer. Finance is left with an amount in the log and no clean evidence of what was bought.


### Purchases cannot be matched to the right project


"Materials" is not enough when several jobs are live. Finance needs the site, purpose, and correct category.


[Petty cash expense heads](https://www.alaan.com/blog/petty-cash-expenses-heads-guide) help with categorisation, but project coding matters just as much. AED 350 booked correctly as repairs is still wrong if it belongs to Site B and lands on Site A.


### Top-ups arrive before the last float is reconciled


The site asks for another AED 5,000 while AED 1,200 from the previous float is still "receipt pending". Repeat that a few times and finance is reconstructing overlapping balances instead of reconciling one float.


### Cash changes hands with no record


The custodian gives cash to whoever is going to the supplier. That is normal site behaviour, but the handover still needs the person, amount, and purpose recorded.


### Personal and site spending get mixed


Someone pays personally, then takes the same amount from the float later, or a purchase contains both site and personal items. Usually it is convenience rather than misconduct, but finance still has to untangle it.


Amarnath Shankaranarayanan, Finance Manager at[K4 Technical Services](https://www.alaan.com/customer-stories/k4) , described "minor, yet frequent discrepancies in the petty cash fund" as evidence that the process needed fixing.


## Controls that survive site conditions


A useful site control has one test: will a busy foreman actually do it?


### Name one custodian per site


Give each float one accountable owner. One accountable owner means finance knows who to ask when a receipt is missing. If cash goes to someone else, record who took it, how much, and why.


### Size the float to roughly a week


A smaller float means more frequent reconciliation, while people still remember what was bought. Base it on your actual cash-only spend, plus a buffer.


### Photograph the receipt when the purchase happens


Receipts get lost in pockets and gloveboxes, and the buyer has often moved to another job by the time finance asks. Capture the image and project tag at purchase.


Alaan has seen the same problem in property operations.[AirDXB's customer story](https://www.alaan.com/customer-stories/airdxb) describes teams across procurement, fit-out, design, and maintenance buying daily consumables and repairs across multiple locations while finance handled the cash and later reconciliation.


### Reconcile before routine top-ups


Topping up an unreconciled float stacks balances and hides shortfalls. Make it a policy rule, with a recorded exception route for genuine emergencies so “urgent” doesn’t become the norm.


## What the auditor and the FTA will want


A defensible site record should let another person reconstruct the purchase: supplier, date, amount, VAT, description, project, and supporting invoice or receipt.


For VAT, a cash receipt is not automatically a tax invoice. The[FTA's guidance on cash receipts and VAT invoices](https://tax.gov.ae/en/faq.aspx?keyword=Will+it+be+possible+to+issue+cash+receipts+instead+of+VAT+invoices%3F) says a valid tax invoice is required for a taxable supply, although a simplified invoice may be used in specified cases.


For a VAT-registered recipient, a simplified tax invoice can be used where the consideration does not exceed AED 10,000. Under[Article 59 of the VAT Executive Regulation](https://tax.gov.ae/DataFolder/Files/Legislation/Executive-Regulation-of-Federal-Decree-Law-No-08-of-2017-Publish-18-09-2025.pdf) , it still needs the supplier's name, address, and TRN, the issue date, a description, total consideration, and VAT charged in AED.


So handwriting itself is not the issue. A handwritten invoice may qualify if it contains the required details. A slip saying only "materials, AED 280" does not.


Input tax recovery also depends on receiving and retaining the relevant tax invoice under[Article 55 of the UAE VAT law](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Legislation/2025/Federal-Decree-Law-No-8-of-2017-and-amendments.pdf) . The FTA says VAT invoices should generally be kept for at least[five years](https://tax.gov.ae/en/faq.aspx?keyword=How+long+must+a+taxable+person+retain+VAT+invoices+for%3F) . For the document itself, see our guide to[itemised receipts](https://www.alaan.com/blog/what-are-itemized-receipts) .


## Replacing the float


The useful petty cash alternatives keep urgent buying possible while moving most site spend onto a traceable payment method.


A site card can sit with an authorised person, carry a defined limit, and create a transaction record as soon as money is spent. The receipt can be uploaded from a phone.


That is where[petty cash management software](https://www.alaan.com/services/petty-cash-management-software) and controlled[corporate cards](https://www.alaan.com/products/corporate-cards) make sense. The general float becomes controlled spend with a transaction record already attached.


K4 Technical Services says it reduced its dependence on petty cash by 90% after moving employees onto Alaan cards with limits and restrictions, alongside automated receipt tracking.


Cash-only suppliers still exist. The honest target is a smaller exception float for purchases that genuinely require cash, with cards used where suppliers accept them.


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the rules for petty cash in the UAE?


Cash purchases do not sit outside the normal VAT documentation rules. For input VAT recovery, keep the appropriate tax invoice and meet the other recovery conditions. Your petty cash policy should cover custodians, limits, handovers, project coding, receipt capture, reconciliation, and top-ups.


### How do you manage petty cash on a construction site?


Use one named custodian, keep the float small, record handovers, photograph receipts at purchase, code spend to the right project, and reconcile before the next routine top-up.


### What should you do about missing receipts?


Record the supplier, date, amount, purpose, and project while the purchase is fresh, then ask for a replacement tax invoice. An internal note can explain what happened, but it does not automatically replace the invoice needed for input VAT recovery.


### Can cards replace petty cash on construction sites?


Cards can replace much of the float where suppliers accept them. They give finance a transaction record immediately and let the user attach the receipt from a phone. Keep a smaller cash float for genuine cash-only purchases.
